Web Sockets are a tunneling layer, and relatively new. The idea is that like the tin cans of your childhood, it tunnels the content to the other side. Encryption masks that data so no one can see what the data really says. However, the downside is only one websocket port can ever be open at once which makes it limited for very large multiple room instance messengers. So if you have two conversations you would need to ping second conversation when you go back to it about what you missed, since theres no mechanism to background retrieve messages

Multicast is not supported by most virtual networks (i have my own theories why), but is supported on local routers and home networks depending on router. Multicast means that you have a local port that acts as a "room". From there people can subscribe to this port, and join in to a conversation locally. Your messages never leave the local network.
